# AI Agent Statistics 2026: Adoption, Spend, Reliability and Failure Rates

Source: https://lowob.com/research/ai-agent-statistics-2026/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-11-16 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Strategy

> Summary: Agents are now common in large companies but rarely run alone. Surveys put agents in production at most large US firms, while McKinsey finds about two in ten respondents scaling agents enterprise-wide. Independent measurements show long tasks completed at 50% success and much shorter ones at 80%, and Gartner expects over 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by the end of 2027. Every figure here carries its source, sample and date.

In 2026, AI agents are common in large companies but rarely run alone: 71% of US enterprise leaders in Zapier's September 2026 survey report agents in production, while McKinsey finds only about two in ten respondents scaling agents enterprise-wide. Spending forecasts run into hundreds of billions of dollars, reliability falls sharply on longer tasks, and Gartner expects over 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by the end of 2027.

*Figure: Agents are the reasoning layer, and they touch every stage of the build.*

This page collects the AI agent statistics most often quoted in 2026 and gives each one its source, sample and date. It supports our hub piece, [What Is an AI Agent?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-agent/), which sets out the definition used here: a model working in a loop toward a goal, choosing its next step and acting through tools within set limits.

Two warnings before the numbers. First, "agent" and "in production" mean different things in each survey, so adoption figures do not add up across sources. Second, many of the most quoted figures come from vendors and investors with a stake in agent adoption. We label each one.

## How many companies use AI agents in 2026?

Most large US companies say they run at least one agent, but few run agents at scale. Zapier's 71% and KPMG's 62% describe presence; McKinsey's "about two in ten" enterprise-wide figure describes depth.

The gap is size as much as definition. McKinsey found 40% of large organisations scaling agents in at least one function against 22% of smaller ones, and the smaller group did not move year on year. Gartner's 2025 survey of IT application leaders shows how cautious most deployments are: 75% had some form of agent in pilot or production, but only 15% were even considering fully autonomous agents.

Among small firms, the C\_TEC survey found 24% of AI users using agentic AI tools. The Stanford AI Index 2026, drawing on McKinsey's 2025 data, found scaled agent use in single digits for nearly all business functions.

## How much are companies spending on AI agents?

Gartner's forecast is the only figure here that is specific to agent software: $206.5 billion in 2026, up from $86.4 billion in 2025. Menlo Ventures does not give a separate agent figure. Its $176.8 billion covers all enterprise spending on using AI, split into $99.5 billion of infrastructure and $77.3 billion of applications.

Menlo's own numbers need care. Its December 2025 report put 2025 enterprise generative AI spend at $37 billion; its November 2026 report gives the prior year's deployment spend as $33 billion, after reclassifying some vendors, and does not reconcile the two. Quote whichever you use with its date and definition, and do not compare across the two reports as if they measured the same thing.

## How reliable are AI agents in 2026?

Reliability is the weakest number in the set. METR's 50% time horizon for Claude Opus 4.5 was about 320 minutes in January 2026, but the 95% interval runs from 170 to 729 minutes, and METR's earlier study found 80% horizons roughly five times shorter. A task an agent finishes half the time is a draft, not a delegated job.

Business-task benchmarks are lower still. Salesforce AI Research's CRMArena-Pro found leading agents at about 58% success on single-turn tasks and about 35% when the task ran over several turns. The researchers also reported near-zero inherent awareness of confidentiality. Our explainer [What Is an AI Time Horizon?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-time-horizon/) covers the method.

## What share of AI agent projects fail?

No source measures agent project failure directly in 2026. The closest figures are a forecast and a survey of AI projects in general. Gartner expects over 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by the end of 2027, citing escalating costs and unclear business value. S&P Global's 451 Research found 42% of companies abandoning most AI initiatives before production, with the average organisation scrapping 46% of proofs of concept.

Value evidence is thin. McKinsey found 37% of respondents attributing any EBIT impact to AI in 2026, essentially unchanged from the year before. Our analysis in [Why AI Agent Projects Fail](https://lowob.com/research/why-ai-agent-projects-fail/) maps these figures to causes.

## How should you read AI agent statistics?

Treat each figure as an answer to the question its survey asked, not as a market fact.

| Check | What to look for | Example from this page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who ran it | Vendor, investor, consultancy, analyst, government or academic | Zapier sells automation; Menlo invests in AI companies |
| Who answered | Size, country and role of respondents | Zapier: US firms with 1,000+ staff; C\_TEC: under 250 staff |
| What "agent" meant | Any AI tool, an assistant with actions, or a goal-seeking loop | KPMG counts "building, deploying or developing" |
| Measured or expected | Observed results or stated expectations | Gartner's 40% cancellation figure is a forecast |
| When | Fieldwork dates, not only publication dates | S&P Global's 42% was fielded in late 2024 |

Our [AI Agent Task Directory](https://lowob.com/research/what-ai-agents-can-do-task-directory/) rates none of its sixty commercial tasks for an agent acting alone, and that is consistent with every reliability figure above.

## lowob takeaways

- **Presence is high, depth is low.** Most large US firms report an agent somewhere; about two in ten scale agents enterprise-wide.
- **Spend figures measure different things.** Gartner forecasts agent software; Menlo estimates all enterprise AI use, and its two reports give different 2025 figures.
- **Plan around the reliable number.** The 80% time horizons are roughly a fifth of the 50% figure, and multi-turn business tasks score lower still.
- **Failure data is mostly forecast.** Gartner's cancellation figure and S&P Global's abandonment rate are the strongest signals, and neither is agent-specific measurement.

## Common questions

### How many companies use AI agents in 2026?

It depends on the survey. Zapier's September 2026 survey of US firms with 1,000 or more employees found 71% with agents in production. KPMG found 62% of US leaders at $1 billion-plus firms building, deploying or developing agents. McKinsey found about two in ten respondents scaling agents across the enterprise, which is the better measure of real depth.

### How much will companies spend on AI agents in 2026?

Gartner forecast AI agent software spending of $206.5 billion in 2026 and $376.3 billion in 2027, up from $86.4 billion in 2025, in a release dated 5 May 2026. Menlo Ventures estimated $176.8 billion of enterprise spending on using AI as of September 2026, but that covers all AI use, not agents alone.

### How reliable are AI agents in 2026?

METR measured Claude Opus 4.5 at about 320 minutes of expert software work at 50% success in January 2026, and its earlier study found 80% horizons roughly five times shorter. On Salesforce AI Research's CRMArena-Pro business benchmark, leading agents reached about 58% on single-turn tasks and about 35% on multi-turn tasks.

### What percentage of AI agent projects fail?

Gartner forecast in June 2025 that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, citing escalating costs and unclear business value. S&P Global's 451 Research found 42% of companies abandoning most AI initiatives before production. Neither is a measured failure rate for agents specifically, so quote them as a forecast and a general AI figure.

### Are AI agent statistics from vendors reliable?

Use them with labels. Vendor and investor surveys often sample firms already interested in the product and define "agent" broadly. Check who ran the survey, who answered, how "agent" was defined, whether results were measured or expected, and when fieldwork happened. Prefer analyst, government and academic figures when they answer the same question.
